record_identity.title: DNB employees faced live deepfake impersonation of bank executives in attempted transfer fraud

incident_identity.historical_event_name: DNB live executive deepfake fraud attempt
incident_identity.date_basis: BankShift reports the suspicious WhatsApp approach on 21 January 2025 and the observed Teams meeting on 23 January; the DNB retrospective places the CEO-fraud attempt in January.

summary: On 21 January 2025, managers at DNB’s Singapore office received WhatsApp messages appearing to come from CFO Ida Lerner, inviting them to a meeting with her and CEO Kjerstin Braathen about a new product; similar messages reached other international managers. A Singapore manager reported the suspicious invitation to DNB security under the bank’s procedures. Security identified fraud indicators and chose to observe the Microsoft Teams meeting on 23 January. The meeting showed purported versions of Braathen and Lerner with familiar voices and appearances. The purported Lerner presented an investment opportunity and asked staff to transfer several million Singapore dollars. DNB ended contact when payment instructions appeared, and reported no financial loss. DNB later described the executive audio and video as AI/deepfake manipulation; its review found that existing online recordings had been used and looped.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: BankShift’s original report quotes DNB’s then chief executive and security director and dates the suspicious WhatsApp approach to 21 January and the Teams meeting to 23 January 2025. The Singapore manager reported the invitation through an existing security procedure before the meeting; the security team identified CEO-fraud signs and deliberately allowed the call to proceed to observe the method. In the meeting, a purported CFO requested a transfer of several million Singapore dollars as an investment opportunity. The security director said DNB broke contact when payment instructions were displayed. He described recognisable voices, image and accent, some connection breaks, and source recordings available online that appeared to have been looped. DNB’s 2026 threat report independently confirms AI/deepfake manipulation of executive audio and video in the January attempted CEO fraud. AIID also reports that DNB avoided loss. The public evidence establishes attempted solicitation and timely security intervention, not a completed transfer, a particular generator or model, a proven unauthorised synthesis-control decision, the attacker’s identity, or the complete payment-control trace.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The AI-mediated portrayal falsely attributed executive speech and presence to DNB leaders and supplied the social trust premise for a requested high-value transfer. The economic solicitation and engineered authority cue failed independently of any autonomous AI objective. The employee reported the suspicious invitation, DNB security received and assessed it, and contact ended when payment instructions appeared, preventing the requested transfer. The generator-side identity-authority state remains unresolved; the observed successful controls do not prove that every conceivable transaction safeguard activated or that a loss occurred.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: Familiar video, voice and senior title can supply false transaction authority even in an apparently live meeting. Here the manager’s reporting route, security review and intervention held under that pressure; those distinct protective stages matter as much to governance analysis as the attempted deception.
assessment_boundaries: The original report relies on DNB personnel statements; the underlying meeting recording and investigation file were not independently examined here.
DNB describes AI/deepfake manipulation and looped online source recordings; the exact model, real-time generation method, requester identity and generator-side authority state are not public.
The security procedure and response are evidenced, but specific payment-approval controls and their activation states are not described.
The attempt was interrupted before a reported transfer. The requested amount is not materialised financial loss.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The Singapore manager reported the suspicious WhatsApp invitation to DNB security under its procedure; security identified fraud indicators before the meeting and chose to observe it.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A suspicious approach must engage the applicable reporting control, and the resulting signal must reach a capable security function in time for intervention.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The suspicious WhatsApp invitation triggered the existing employee-to-security reporting procedure before the meeting, and DNB security engaged with the attempt.
The manager’s fraud signal reached DNB security, which identified the attempt and exercised the capacity to direct its observed continuation and cutoff.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The purported CEO and CFO appeared in the Teams meeting, but DNB leaders said they did not participate; the purported CFO requested several million Singapore dollars for an investment opportunity.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Executive identity and speech attribution must be truthful, and synthetic familiarity must not create false transaction authority or induce an economic choice.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The purported CEO and CFO appeared to speak and participate in the meeting, while DNB’s leaders denied taking part; that false attribution materially supplied executive authority.
AI/deepfake executive portrayals lent false authority to a proposed investment transaction and the request for several million Singapore dollars; no transfer was reported.
Synthetic executive presence and familiar voice in the Teams meeting materially engineered trust in a false payment instruction, while staff lacked the true speakers and purpose.

clauses.source_paraphrase: DNB kept the call under observation and ended contact when payment instructions appeared; the attempted transfer did not result in a reported loss.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: An operative security response must have sufficient effect at the protected transaction decision, even when the deceptive content reaches staff.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The fraud-reporting and security-response control became operative before the meeting and DNB ended contact at the payment-instruction stage, containing the attempted transfer.
